A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Differential RL work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the DPO-to-dfPO renaming and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on surface modeling, grid-based modeling, and octa-alanine molecular dynamics, including benchmark costs, trajectories, and statistics across 10 seeds.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds baseline hyperparameter ablations, classic-control evaluations, and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Hamiltonian-gradient policy, stage-wise sampling, replay targets, smooth L1 training, and automatic differentiation. DPO becomes dfPO, but neither this renaming nor the expanded control-theory explanations changes the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds actual evaluations on continuous-state/action Pendulum, Mountain Car, and CartPole, extending coverage beyond the three retained scientific-computing tasks. The additional application examples in Appendix C.6 are explanatory, rather than further evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The scientific comparisons retain TRPO, PPO, DDPG, SAC, CrossQ, and TQC in both standard and reward-shaped forms. The new classic-control comparison uses these existing algorithm families; the ablations vary their settings without introducing new comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: New experiments vary critic counts, quantiles, entropy coefficients, action noise, target updates, clipping, advantage normalization, and GAE settings. Appendix C.5 also introduces continuous-action classic-control protocols with explicitly modified Mountain Car and CartPole rewards. The original scientific-task budgets, horizons, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 2 and 5 add extensive sensitivity analyses across all six baseline families and both reward formulations, testing whether dfPO's advantage survives different comparator hyperparameters. dfPO itself remains at fixed defaults, so these are checks of comparative robustness rather than ablations of its components or hyperparameters.

E5.justification: The retained benchmark analysis uses the same 10 seeds, over 200 test episodes per seed, mean ± standard deviation reporting, and seed-level t-tests, including the same Surface/CrossQ exception. The new tables do not disclose an additional uncertainty procedure or increased repetition count.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain their numerical results, while Figure 1's surface-modeling trajectories change. New Tables 2, 5, 7, and 8 report ablation costs, training times, and classic-control rewards. In Table 8, dfPO leads CartPole with 0.1352, while TRPO leads Pendulum and TQC leads Mountain Car; these are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: v3 Lemma B.6 becomes v4 Lemma B.7 and strengthens p >= d to p >= 2d for the O(epsilon^-6) result. Its proof corrects the sample scaling to O(epsilon^-1), introduces delta_k = k delta/d, and repairs probability bookkeeping. Equation (19) also replaces the training-sample count with the discretization-step count. New Appendices D and E add Hamiltonian/HJB/TD derivations and an exceptional-set argument for linear boundedness.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same framework, pointwise-convergence claim, O(K^5/6) headline regret rate, and superiority claim on the three scientific-computing tasks. The additional evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations connecting its score function to Hamiltonian, continuous-time q, and TD quantities; motivates the representative tasks; and explains why adaptive PDE solvers can make intermediate restarting impractical. It also discusses linear boundedness for analytic functions and interprets the new sensitivity and classic-control results. The original limitations discussion is retained as Appendix F.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies dfPO's learning rate of 0.001 and batch size of 32, provides approximate training times in Table 7, and documents the new Gym reward formulas. The A100 hardware disclosure and original model-size information remain. The repository pointer is updated, while trained-artifact access instructions remain described in the checklist.

R1.justification: New Section 5 substantially expands positioning against continuous-time RL, including work by Ainsworth, Wang, Jia and Zhou, Yildiz, and Zhao. It distinguishes discretizing the differential dual and using the extended state-adjoint space, and compares regret guarantees under different assumptions with work including Maran and Vakili–Olkhovskaya.

P1.justification: v4 substantially expands explanatory prose through a dedicated related-work section, task motivation, physics intuition, and assumptions discussion. It reorganizes experimental appendices and the proof presentation, including extracting an existing gradient-complexity argument into a separate lemma, and adds the NeurIPS checklist. Terminology and Hamiltonian/time-step notation are standardized throughout.

P2.justification: v4 adds two extensive grouped ablation tables, a training-time table, and a classic-control results table. Figure 1 is revised, including changed surface-panel curves and vertical scale. Existing benchmark, task-setting, statistics, and model-size tables are retained with layout or placement adjustments, and Algorithm 1 moves to the following page.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens support for the paper by testing dependence on baseline hyperparameters, correcting visible scaling and probability errors, and stating the stronger assumption supporting the special-case rate. Section 5 also addresses the earlier lack of detailed positioning against continuous-time RL. The mixed classic-control results help assess applicability, although their modified rewards and limited budget/uncertainty documentation constrain that evidence. These gains improve empirical credibility and theoretical precision despite the unchanged algorithm and primary benchmark scores.
